text: Large language models (LLMs) are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at tasks like summarising texts, answering questions and translating languages. However, they also have limits. They sometimes give wrong information, cannot truly understand meaning, and may repeat biases found in their training data. For these reasons, we should always check their answers carefully.
